name: The Threshold of Machine Authorship
title: The Threshold of Machine Authorship
answer: The threshold of machine authorship is the line between a human created work and an output that a copyright system will treat as authorless. It covers registration claims, ownership disputes, infringement defenses, and disclosure duties when generative systems produce text, images, code, or music. The site tracks 148 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, and 29 AI case law precedents, which give the threshold its current shape. The question is not whether a machine can generate expression, but whether a human contributed enough protected expression to claim authorship. That boundary also affects contracts, licenses, and the value of works that mix human and machine contributions.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: The threshold of machine authorship is the line between a human created work and an output that a copyright system will treat as authorless. It covers registration claims, ownership disputes, infringement defenses, and disclosure duties when generative systems produce text, images, code, or music. The site tracks 148 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, and 29 AI case law precedents, which give the threshold its current shape. The question is not whether a machine can generate expression, but whether a human contributed enough protected expression to claim authorship. That boundary also affects contracts, licenses, and the value of works that mix human and machine contributions.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The threshold runs on a patchwork of copyright statutes, registration practices, court dockets, and state legislation. Copyright offices publish guidance and examination manuals, while courts apply those rules case by case. The site's 219 compliance and regulation pages and 6,978 state AI bills show how many jurisdictions are adding disclosure and provenance requirements. Practitioners also rely on dockets, pleadings, registration records, and agency correspondence to see how the threshold is applied. No single database settles the question, so the working infrastructure is part legal text, part administrative record, and part litigation history.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done by comparing the human contribution to the machine output at each step of creation. Analysts review prompts, revisions, selections, arrangements, and edits to decide whether a person exercised creative control. They also examine registration statements, deposit copies, and disclosures to see what was claimed and what was omitted. Courts and agencies often look for a human author who conceived the work and used the tool as an instrument. The method is documentary and comparative, not purely technical, because the legal question turns on control and intent rather than model architecture.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk turn on provenance, ownership, and disclosure. If a work lacks sufficient human authorship, registration may be refused or canceled, and infringement claims may weaken. If a work mixes human and machine contributions, contracts and licenses often define who owns what and what happens if the human contribution is later questioned. Provenance records, model terms, and disclosure statements become evidence of how the output was made, and downstream users face risk when they cannot show a clean chain of title. The site's 92 intellectual property lawsuits among 148 active AI lawsuits show that these disputes are already being tested.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The threshold is moving as more registration decisions, court rulings, and state bills accumulate. Expect more attention to disclosure, provenance metadata, and the recordkeeping that supports authorship claims. The vocabulary is still settling, which is why the site maintains 686 glossary terms and tracks 732 AI tools alongside its case law. Future disputes may focus less on whether a machine generated something and more on how much human selection, arrangement, and revision the law will recognize. The direction is toward clearer documentation requirements and more granular tests for human contribution.
